article_title: Multi-source feedback in undergraduate medical education: a pilot study.
citation: Bartman I, St-Onge C, Roy M, Gingerich A, Katsoulas E, Chahine S, Gagnon N. (2025). Multi-source feedback in undergraduate medical education: a pilot study. Canadian Medical Education Journal. https://doi.org/10.36834/cmej.79283
title: R2C2 feedback and coaching model: building relationship, exploring reactions and content, and coaching for performance change
description: The R2C2 model is an evidence- and theory-based facilitated feedback model the article used to train the pilot's facilitators. It structures a one-on-one feedback conversation so that the recipient critically reflects on a performance report and converts that reflection into improvement plans. The article states that 'The R2C2 feedback and coaching model aimed to promote the recipient's critical reflection on their performance report and, through that, identify opportunities for improvement and develop a plan for addressing them.' In the pilot, facilitators trained in R2C2 led minimum 30-minute sessions reviewing each student's individualized MSF report.
requirements: Facilitators must receive training in the R2C2 model
A safe environment for feedback reception, with facilitators who have no influence over the learner's promotion
target_learners: medical trainees receiving multisource feedback reports
examples: Pilot facilitators were faculty members with no influence over clerk promotion, trained in R2C2, and met students for at least 30 minutes
